blogs.title: When Angioedema Isn’t: Dermatomyositis in the Differential of Neck Swelling
blogs.description: A case-based review of pseudoangioedema in dermatomyositis, focusing on how inflammatory cervical edema can mimic Ludwig angina, deep neck space infection, or idiopathic angioedema. The post would emphasize red flags for non-histaminergic, non-bradykinin swelling and offer a practical diagnostic approach for ED, ENT, and acute medicine clinicians when the usual angioedema story does not fit.

blogs.title: The CK That Changed the Case: Bedside Clues to Occult Inflammatory Myopathy
blogs.description: This post would highlight the small findings that prevented diagnostic anchoring: proximal weakness, periungual changes, nailfold capillary abnormalities, atypical facial erythema, and unexplained AST/ALT elevation. It would argue for early creatine kinase testing in patients with unexplained edema plus subtle neuromuscular or dermatologic findings, and discuss how 'transaminitis' may actually be muscle injury.

blogs.title: Swelling, Dysphagia, and Silent Aspiration: Airway and Swallowing Pitfalls in Dermatomyositis
blogs.description: Using this case, the blog would explore dysphagia as a high-stakes manifestation of inflammatory myopathy, including when airway symptoms are due to pharyngeal muscle involvement rather than structural ENT disease. It would cover bedside recognition, indications for swallow studies, aspiration risk, nutritional planning, and why severe dysphagia should push clinicians toward urgent treatment.

blogs.title: SAE1-Positive Dermatomyositis: What the Antibody Adds Beyond the Diagnosis
blogs.description: A focused review of the anti-SAE1 phenotype, including its associations with prominent cutaneous disease, dysphagia, interstitial lung disease, edema, and malignancy risk. The post would discuss how myositis-specific antibodies, MRI, PET, and muscle biopsy complement each other, and where serology meaningfully informs prognosis and surveillance rather than simply confirming dermatomyositis.

blogs.title: Treating Severe Dermatomyositis Up Front: Why This Was More Than a Steroid-Only Disease
blogs.description: This post would examine the rationale for aggressive early combination therapy in severe dermatomyositis with neck muscle involvement and major dysphagia. It would review the practical decision-making behind pulse methylprednisolone, IVIG, mycophenolate, rituximab, and PJP prophylaxis, including how clinicians choose steroid-sparing agents when lung involvement is a concern and evidence is limited.

blogs.title: Cancer Screening in Dermatomyositis: Applying Risk-Stratified Surveillance at the Bedside
blogs.description: A teaching post on malignancy screening in dermatomyositis, using this patient’s SAE1 positivity, dysphagia, male sex, and dermatomyositis diagnosis to illustrate IMACS-style risk stratification. It would discuss how to balance CT, PET, age-appropriate screening, endoscopy, and longitudinal follow-up without overtesting, while acknowledging that a negative initial screen does not end the story.
